slides.title: Mental Health Is Health
slides.content: Mental health exists on a spectrum: Thriving Coping Struggling In Crisis Everyone moves along this spectrum throughout the year. Mental health is affected by: Sleep Money People Workload Home life Physical activity Struggling is information, not weakness.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'Mental Health Is Health'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on Mental Health Is Health.

slides.title: Recognising Stress
slides.content: Signs of stress can include: Trouble starting work. Trouble stopping work. Changes in sleep. Irritability. Avoidance. Falling behind with coursework or portfolios. Common causes include: Deadlines. Workload. Financial pressures. Home pressures. Balancing study and work.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'Recognising Stress'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on Recognising Stress.

slides.title: What Actually Helps Stress
slides.content: Evidence-based strategies include: Move: Regular physical activity, even walking. Connect: Spending time with people. Sleep: Protecting healthy sleep habits. Talk: Speaking to somebody about what is happening.

exercise.prompt: What is a key message of 'What Actually Helps Stress'?
options: It is only assessed in exams
It applies only to certain students

It is optional and not required
exercise.explanation: Evidence-based strategies include: Move: Regular physical activity, even walking

slides.title: Sleep Is a Study Tool
slides.content: Sleep affects: Memory. Concentration. Focus. Emotional regulation. Good sleep habits include: Consistent wake-up times. Limiting screen use before bed. Reducing caffeine later in the day. Revision and learning depend on sleep for memory consolidation.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'Sleep Is a Study Tool'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on Sleep Is a Study Tool.

slides.title: Money Can Affect Wellbeing
slides.content: Financial stress can affect: Mood. Sleep. Attendance. Concentration. Motivation. Students should know that support such as hardship funding exists and that asking for help is normal.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Money Can Affect Wellbeing'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Money Can Affect Wellbeing.

slides.title: Support Routes Exist
slides.content: The support process is: 1. Tell someone. 2. Referral is made. 3. Appropriate support is arranged. You can approach: Tutors. Teachers. Wellbeing staff. Support services. Any trusted adult can be the starting point.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Support Routes Exist'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Support Routes Exist.

slides.title: Tell College What It Needs to Know
slides.content: Inform the college about: Disabilities. Learning needs. Mental health conditions. Circumstances affecting study. Support can only be arranged when the college is aware of the need.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Tell College What It Needs to Know'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Tell College What It Needs to Know.

slides.title: Look Out For Others
slides.content: The process is simple: Changes in behaviour. "Are you actually okay?" A trusted adult if serious support is needed. Helping someone get support is not betrayal.

exercise.prompt: What is a key message of 'Look Out For Others'?
options: It is only assessed in exams
It applies only to certain students
It is optional and not required
The process is simple: Changes in behaviour
exercise.explanation: The process is simple: Changes in behaviour

slides.content: Key points to remember: Mental health is health Learn to recognise stress Prioritise sleep Understand support routes Ask for help early Notice and support peers
